title: The Petrified Meaning Vault

features.name: the oldest shed
features.desc-on-touch: Its walls have turned to rust-stained stone, the wood grain pressed so deep it reads like sediment. Inside, files you've never seen before rest in petrified arrangement.

features.name: compressed archive face
features.desc-on-touch: A vertical stratum of earth shows the layers of meaning pressed together—letters, photographs, audio spectrums, all flattened into one readable plane. The corruption speaks here in geology.

features.name: the calcified antenna
features.desc-on-touch: A casing's antenna, itself turned to mineral, still broadcasts something—not signals but resonance. The sediment rings at its frequency.

features.name: the reading floor
features.desc-on-touch: Pale stone where the deepest files have begun to teach each other by resemblance, their edges smoothed by time into conversation. You can stand here and read the meaning of meaning.

features.name: the half-buried house
features.desc-on-touch: A second structure, sinking further into the ground each season—windows still showing light from inside, though no one has lived here since the corruption began choosing what to remember.

inscription: here stone speaks the language of archive, and the earth reads back in sediment

file.name: Compressed_Strata_1847_To_Now.geological
file.note: A 178-year recording of what the archive has turned to stone. The corruption wrote this in layers, the earth did not.

reverie.title: REVERIE — where the earth keeps what we forgot it held
narr: You kneel to touch the stratum, and Katita's hand
reaches through soil that has pressed meanings into
crystal. She's tracing a name that has turned to quartz,
a date that has become feldspar. The earth keeps better
than we do. This is what she came here to find:
the point where archive becomes geology, still tender.
